sessionTitle: Create enterprise AI apps at scale with Bolt and Microsoft

announcements.name: Bolt integration with Microsoft Copilot
announcements.shortDescription: Teams can structure a project brief in Microsoft Copilot and tag the Bolt agent directly to send specifications over and trigger a build without losing requirements.
announcements.longDescription: Work starts in Microsoft Copilot, where a team turns a conversation, set of requirements, or early product idea into a clear project brief, including goals, audience, user needs, constraints, success criteria, and brand requirements. After iterating on the plan (for example optimizing for SEO), the team tags the Bolt agent to summarize the conversation into a prompt and asks it to build with those specifications. Copilot connects directly with Bolt, and selecting "Build" sends the prompt over so the project starts building. The demo shows Bolt creating the project with a full hero carousel focusing on images as requested.

announcements.name: Bolt CLI for programmatic interaction
announcements.shortDescription: Developers can bundle a local component library, connect existing repos and workflows, and publish an approved design system into Bolt.
announcements.longDescription: The Bolt command line interface gives developers a programmatic way to interact with Bolt. They can bring in approved assets, connect existing repos and workflows, and make the organization's technical standards available to the broader team. This is one of three pieces covered in the demo, alongside design systems and the Bolt interface, supporting a controlled path from idea to application while preserving governance and developer standards.

announcements.name: Design systems as a shared foundation
announcements.shortDescription: Bolt can ingest code, design artifacts, and documentation to generate a navigable Storybook instance so new projects start from approved components rather than a blank canvas.
announcements.longDescription: Using the Bolt CLI, a developer can bundle and create a design system from a local component library, sending code, design artifacts, and documentation to a Bolt Agent. Bolt makes sense of the code and design components so the team can build new applications, prototypes, or internal apps on top of that existing material. The core value is reducing the non-deterministic qualities of agents and giving back control over what code is produced and used. The demo prompts via Copilot to create a design system and publish it within Bolt, then views it at bolt.new under Settings.

announcements.name: Plan mode
announcements.shortDescription: An agent mode that previews what will be implemented before building, intended to save time and tokens.
announcements.longDescription: After selecting a model (Opus 4.7 [inferred, "modal" is a mishearing of "model"]), the user puts the request into plan mode and builds. Plan mode is a way to see what the agent wants to implement before it actually does so, often saving time and tokens. In the demo the Bolt Agent generates a plan to set up a database with authentication and a plan-a-trip modal; because it asks no clarifying questions, the user proceeds to implement.

announcements.name: Built-in database security scan
announcements.shortDescription: Projects can be scanned for issues before publishing directly to a live site.
announcements.longDescription: Before publishing a project directly to a live site, Bolt offers an inbuilt database security scan. In the demo the scan shows no issues, so the team proceeds to publish and view the live site, ready for customers. This caps off a workflow where a server function calling the OpenAI API was created to generate a travel itinerary.
